scenes.text: Same AI, same question. So why do some people get amazing answers, while others get total junk? [1] Here's the secret, it's all in the prompt. [2] So in this episode, let's talk about prompt engineering.

title: Prompt
Engineering
data.subtitle: Talk to AI like a pro

scenes.text: A prompt is simply the instruction you give an AI. [1] And prompt engineering just means writing that instruction clearly, so the AI knows exactly what you want. When you do that, [2] your input gets better, [3] your answers get better, [4] and you spend a lot less time retrying.

data.definition: Writing clear instructions so the AI knows exactly what you want.

scenes.text: Let me show you. [1] Here's a lazy prompt, write about my product. And look at the reply, it's vague and generic. [2] Now let's build a better one, step by step. First, give it a role, you are an expert marketer. [3] Then some context, my brand sells handmade coconut soaps from Kerala. [4] Next, the actual task, write an Instagram caption for our new jasmine soap. [5] And finally, the format, under forty words, friendly, with three hashtags. [6] And now, the reply is exactly what we wanted.

scenes.text: Here are four power moves you can use today. [1] First, give examples. Show it one or two samples of what you want, and that's called few shot prompting. [2] Second, for maths or logic, ask it to think step by step. [3] Third, set clear limits, like word count, tone, or language. [4] And fourth, iterate. Treat it like a conversation, and keep refining.

So where can you use this in real life? [1] You can get your resume reviewed, the way a recruiter would. [2] You can draft a polite WhatsApp reply to your landlord. [3] Or you can turn messy meeting notes into a clean summary, with action items.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think prompt engineering needs secret magic words. [2] Honestly, it doesn't. It's just clear communication. If a smart new intern would understand your instruction, the AI will understand it too.

data.fact: It's clear communication. If a smart new intern would understand it, so will the AI.
